chunks: Yet when good came their way they said: 'It is our due;' but when misfortune befell them they put the omen down to Moses and those who were with him. But surely the omen was with God, yet most of them did not understand.

key_terms.يَطَّيَّرُوا: They considered it a bad omen

ai.seo_question: How did the Israelites attribute good and bad fortune according to Surah Al-A'raf?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the Israelites' superficial attribution of blessings to their own merit while casting misfortunes as omens linked to Moses, illustrating a lack of deep spiritual insight. The phrase 'their omen is with Allah' signifies that true destiny and divine decree reside solely with God, contrasting with the popular notion of external signs. This reflects the broader theological principle that while humans may perceive events as lucky or unlucky, ultimate control and meaning are derived from the Divine Will.
